relationships.subject: Trpv1-lineage sensory neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: We provide the first evidence that Trpv1-lineage sensory neurons predominantly induce burst firing, a unique mode of neuronal activity, in lamina I spino-PAG projection neurons.

relationships.evidence_quote: LFS of Trpv1+ afferents enhanced the synaptically evoked and intrinsic excitability of spino-PAG projection neurons

relationships.subject: NMDA receptor
relationships.evidence_quote: Further experiments revealed that this plasticity required Trpv1+ afferent input, postsynaptic G protein-coupled signaling, and NMDA receptor activation.

relationships.subject: postsynaptic G protein-coupled signaling
relationships.evidence_quote: this plasticity required Trpv1+ afferent input, postsynaptic G protein-coupled signaling, and NMDA receptor activation

key_findings: Trpv1-lineage primary afferents drive burst firing in lamina I spino-PAG projection neurons, and 2 Hz low-frequency stimulation of these afferents potentiates their synaptic and intrinsic excitability.
This plasticity requires Trpv1+ afferent input, postsynaptic G protein-coupled signaling and NMDA receptor activation, and is reproduced by inflammatory injury and heat exposure in vivo.
